title: Add rolling resilience-curve canary with tiered fallback and rate fallthrough
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a rolling resilience-curve canary that detects gradual, sustained degradations and a tiered fallback policy (soft fallback -> model variant -> rate fallthrough) to limit blast radius during rollouts.
description: Motivation: We observed slow, multi-hour regressions that did not trigger existing spike-focused detectors; this PR adds a time-weighted 'resilience curve' canary that measures cumulative degradation slope across cohorts and triggers tiered safeguards. High level: 1) rolling resilience curve evaluator that computes a decay-weighted degradation area under curve (AUC) for latency and error rate across multiple cohort slices (region, client-class, route). 2) temporal quorum voting: requires consensus from multiple independent cohorts before a hard fallback. 3) tiered fallback policy: soft fallback (traffic shaping + alert only), model-variant fallback (route to a lower-cost stable variant), and rate fallthrough (graceful request shedding with progressive SLAs). 4) adaptive probe scheduling that increases probe frequency for cohorts showing rising AUC and backs off when stabilized. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-18721) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] e2e smoke in perf lab - [x] docs added under docs/perf - [x] fallthrough behavior validated with canary simulator Implementation notes: The resilience curve is implemented in canary/engine/resilience_curve.py with an efficient incremental aggregator and configurable half-life. Voting is implemented as a quorum module that accepts weighted cohort votes. Fallbacks are implemented in alerts/rollout_guard.go and routing/soft_fallback.rs. This PR also adds a canary simulator harness and two smoke tests. Related: builds on prior probe-scheduling work (ENG-17234). Risk/rollback: feature gated behind canary.v2 flag; rollout guard defaults to soft mode until explicitly enabled in the console. Testing: see test/integration/resilience_smoke_test.py and perf-canary lab run id perf-lab-20260212-07. Merge notes: squash-merged to main after addressing review comments and CI fixes.
